_comment: HAND-MAINTAINED decisions about which part a reference designator buys, and why. The exclusion-ledger shape: every entry that is not a plain lookup carries a reason. scripts/check_stock.py joins this with scripts/link_mpn.json (the upstream schematic's own Digi-Key links, resolved once) and with live Digi-Key/Mouser data, and writes pcbway-assembly/resolved-mpns.json. THAT FILE IS GENERATED -- edit this one instead. An override beats a schematic link, which is how an ECO's part swap survives the fact that the upstream schematic still points at the part it replaced.

SWAPPED 2026-08-19 from GRM21BR61E226ME44L, which was at ZERO stock at both distributors with a 17-week lead (verified 2026-08-19). This is the SAME GRM->GRT move made on the 10 uF line, and for the same reason. Verified parameter-by-parameter on the Digi-Key API against the incumbent: capacitance 22 uF, tolerance +/-20%, RATED VOLTAGE 25 V, dielectric X5R, package 0805 (2012 Metric), max thickness 1.45 mm and operating range -55 to +85 C are ALL IDENTICAL. The only difference is that the GRT is Murata's soft-termination series and is AEC-Q200 automotive-qualified, which the GRM is not. Nothing is given up. 2,022 in stock at Digi-Key (verified 2026-08-19) = 674 boards' worth at 3 per board; Mouser has none, so this line is single-sourced. BOM-only: board Value stays `22u`, no board file moves -- but the SCHEMATIC's Source link for these three still points at the GRM and needs the same edit.
CORRECTION TO AN EARLIER ENTRY IN THIS FILE: it previously said 'NO LIKE-FOR-LIKE EXISTS -- every 22 uF 25 V X5R 0805 from a tier-1 maker is at zero', and recommended dropping to a 16 V part. THAT WAS WRONG. It came from a keyword search that filtered on stock >= 5,000, which silently excluded every real 25 V candidate -- all of which sit in the hundreds-to-thousands. A threshold chosen to shorten a search result had turned into a claim about the market. The deep sweep that found this one scanned 1,297 results across 15 query shapes with no stock floor.
entries.alternate:
GRM21BC81E226ME44K if you want depth: Murata, 25 V, 0805, +/-20%, same 1.45 mm max thickness, 7,338 in stock at Digi-Key (verified 2026-08-19) -- 3.6x the fitted part -- and a WIDER temperature range, -55 to +105 C against the X5R's -55 to +85 C. The catch is that it is X6S, a DIFFERENT DIELECTRIC FORMULATION, and DC-bias behaviour is exactly what holding 25 V was meant to protect. I could NOT verify its bias curve against the X5R's: Murata publishes that data only through SimSurfing, whose API returns HTTP 500 from here, and the product PDFs do not carry the curve. So the conservative pick is the part that changes nothing. If you have SimSurfing access, compare the two at 5 V bias and take the better one -- the extra stock is real.
Also checked and REJECTED: ZRA21CR61E226ME01L (Murata, 25 V X5R, 5,330 in stock) looks ideal in a Mouser listing but Digi-Key's parameters give its package as 'Nonstandard SMD' at 1.65 mm thick, not 0805/1.45 mm. It is not a drop-in. KGM21AR51E226MU (Kyocera AVX, 25 V X5R 0805, 612 at Digi-Key + 5 at Mouser, $1.06, 28-week lead) is a genuine second source if both Murata parts dry up.
The 16 V option remains available and is NO LONGER RECOMMENDED, since 25 V is in stock: GRM21BR61C226ME44L, 95,529 at Digi-Key. It costs DC-bias capacitance on C21's 5 V rail, which the component review flagged as mattering. Take it only if every 25 V part above is gone.

entries.note: SWAPPED 2026-08-19 from GRM188R61E106KA73J, which was at ZERO stock at both distributors with a 17-week lead (verified 2026-08-19). BOM-only: the board Value stays `10u` and no board file changes, so unlike ECO-8's Value edits this one cannot be reverted by a PCB-from-schematic sync -- but the SCHEMATIC's own Source link for these seven still points at the GRM, so update it there too before anyone regenerates a BOM from the schematic. Verified parameter-by-parameter against the incumbent on the Digi-Key API: capacitance 10 uF, rated voltage 25 V, dielectric X5R, package 0603 (1608), max thickness 1.00 mm and operating range -55 to +85 C are ALL IDENTICAL. Two differences, both neutral-or-better here: tolerance loosens from +/-10% to +/-20%, which is immaterial on bulk decoupling and is dwarfed by MLCC DC-bias derating anyway; and the GRT is Murata's soft-termination series and is AEC-Q200 automotive-qualified, which the GRM is not. WHY THE VOLTAGE MATTERED MORE THAN THE TOLERANCE: the seven placements sit on VOUT3 (3.228 V), VCC (<=3.2 V), VAUD (2.5 V), VDD2 (2.5 V), U17-VDD and /D1A, and the power review flagged DC-bias derating as the thing to protect. Rated voltage drives derating far harder than the tolerance band does, so holding 25 V and giving up the tolerance grade is the right way round.
entries.alternate: GRT188R61C106KE13D if you want DEPTH and a SECOND SOURCE more than you want the 25 V rating: 10 uF +/-10% 16 V X5R 0603, Digi-Key 764,592 and Mouser 456,339 (verified 2026-08-19), versus the fitted GRT part's 192,299 at Digi-Key and ZERO at Mouser. It also restores the incumbent's +/-10% tolerance. The cost is the one thing this swap was chosen to protect: 16 V instead of 25 V in the same 0603 case means noticeably more capacitance lost to DC bias. Breakdown is not the issue -- the highest of these seven rails is 3.23 V, so 16 V is still 5x headroom.

ECO-8: replaces 10k on both. Cuts the statically-biased brownout-latch current from 389 uA to 81 uA off VBATT. Forced beta stays at 2.4 against hFE minima of 60 (2N3906) and 40 (2N3904). Same part as R12/R17/R64, already on the BOM.

ECO-8: replaces 1k. Cuts the post-brownout latched-off drain from 2.40 mA to 240 uA. Must be paired with R24 = 1M, otherwise /EN falls from 0.990 x SW to 0.909 x SW and Q10B's already-marginal gate drive gets worse.

ECO-8: replaces 100k. Restores the /EN divider ratio alongside R11 = 10k. Verified against the LTC3527 SHDN input current (1 uA typ / 2 uA max): /EN = 2.356 V at SW = 2.4 V and 1.762 V at SW = 1.8 V, both far above the 0.88 V VIH.

ECO-8: replaces 100k on the MIC1553 CS pull-up. 470k not the 1M the review proposed: the MIC1553 datasheet gives no numeric CS leakage spec and warns that a floating CS is unpredictable, and the worst-case CS-high threshold is 0.72 x VS = 3.61 V, not the nominal 2/3.

ECO-10 (proposed in the power review, deferred by ECO-8, applied here). X7R -> C0G. These are the Sallen-Key FEEDBACK caps -- the ones that set Q -- and their partners C26/C31 are already C0G. X7R drifts +/-15% over its range while C0G drifts +/-30ppm/degC, so a handheld warming in the hand detunes half of each filter section and no tolerance grade fixes it.

entries.eco: ECO-13, and the reason this repository exists. On the AGBM-01 base U2 was a salvaged AGB-SRAM off a donor console, and ECO-5 was OUR unverified attempt to let a new part stand in for it. AGBM-02 carries MouseBiteLabs' own dual land, so this is simply an ORDERABLE PART: the machine buys it and places it, and a build needs exactly one chip off a donor -- the CPU. His Required Parts page: "For the AGBM-02 and AGBM-12, you *only* need the CPU." Tape-and-reel suffix chosen over the tube part for machine placement. 8 Mbit 512K x 16 async SRAM, 45 ns, 48-TSOP I. TWO HAND STEPS COME WITH IT and no assembly line does either: bridge JP2 (U2 pin 17 MA17 to GND) and JP3 (pin 47 /BYTE to VDD2 for x16 word mode). Leave BOTH open if you fit a salvaged OEM AGB-SRAM instead -- the land still accepts it, and then this line comes off the BOM. $10.85, 1,695 in stock, verified 2026-08-19.

entries.eco: ECO-12, the wiki audit. The schematic-vs-PCB conflict is SETTLED: the PCB annotation was stale. MouseBiteLabs' AGBM-02 -- the same AA design one revision later, identical supervisor circuit -- carries 5.1k/33k/200k in its own PCB file, and so do the AGBM-01 schematic, the AGBM-01 README BOM and the AGBM-02 README BOM. The wiki then states the resulting thresholds outright ("The low battery LED turns on when the voltage passes 2.3V ... begins blinking when the voltage passes 2.1V") and the AGBM-01 build guide's Test 4 sweeps 2 V to 3 V expecting the green-to-red change at 2.3 V. 5.1k/33k puts it at 2.309 V; 1k/10k puts it at 2.200 V. R3 is U10's top leg. Value corrected 1k -> 5.1k, and it now takes the SAME part as R58 -- U17's top leg -- so both AA supervisor dividers run on one film system. Susumu RG1608: 0.1%, +/-25 ppm, anti-sulfur, AEC-Q200. Anti-sulfur matters here specifically: this divider hangs off SW, inches from two AA cells, and sulfur creep is how a thick-film chip resistor goes open. $0.10, 141,038 in stock, verified 2026-08-19.

R4 is U10's bottom leg. Value corrected 10k -> 33k. Same Susumu RG1608 film as R3 so the RATIO -- which is the whole quantity that sets the trip point -- tracks instead of drifting on two independent films. 0.1% +/-25 ppm against the previous 1% +/-100 ppm takes the trip-point spread from about +/-21 mV to +/-2 mV, which on Nick's own battery curves is the difference between a few minutes of the 20-60 minute low-battery warning and none of it. $0.10, 18,495 in stock, verified 2026-08-19.

R64 is not a divider leg -- it is the 555's timing resistor, and with C44 = 1 uF it sets the critical-battery blink rate: 200k gives 3.6 Hz, the 100k annotation gives 7.2 Hz. Value corrected 100k -> 200k, buying exactly the part the upstream schematic's own Digi-Key link buys. DELIBERATELY LEFT AT 1%: a blink rate does not need 0.1%, and buying precision where it buys nothing is waste -- the same rule that deferred all three of these in ECO-10.

entries.eco: ECO-10, audio precision. These set f0 and Q of the 4th-order Butterworth reconstruction filter (15.84 kHz per channel). 1% +/-100ppm thick film -> 0.1% +/-25ppm thin film. Susumu RG1608 covers every value in the filter, so the whole network is ONE film system and the ratios that set Q track each other instead of drifting independently. ~$0.11 a part.

R58 is not in the filter -- it is the U17 supervisor's upper divider leg, and it gets the same part for the same reason: a trip point should not move with temperature.

ECO-12. U17's lower divider leg. ECO-10 upgraded it to 0.1% but left it on YAGEO RT0603 while its partner R58 went to Susumu RG1608 -- a divider split across two film systems, which is the one thing ECO-10's own reasoning says not to do, since only the RATIO sets the trip point. Now both legs are Susumu RG1608 (0.1%, +/-25 ppm, anti-sulfur, AEC-Q200), matching what R3/R4 do for U10. $0.11, 488,743 in stock, verified 2026-08-19. R55 keeps RT0603BRD07100KL: it is the VOUT3 bottom leg and belongs to the all-YAGEO LTC3527 pair.
ECO-10. Already C0G; tolerance +/-5% -> +/-1%, and AEC-Q200. Q goes as sqrt(Cfb/Cgnd), so tightening the shunt legs tightens the alignment directly.

ECO-10, longevity. The fitted KEMET C0603C105K4RACTU is X7R but only 16 V; TDK's CGA is the AUTOMOTIVE (AEC-Q200) grade of the C-series at 25 V in the same 0603 x 0.90 mm body. Higher rated voltage means less capacitance lost to DC bias on every rail these sit on, and the automotive grade is screened harder. 1,435,431 in stock, $0.17 (verified 2026-08-19). NOT CHANGED, and worth saying why: the 0.1 uF line is already KEMET C0603C104K5RACTU, X7R at 50 V -- that is already the right part and churning it would buy nothing.

ECO-11. NDC7002N VGS(th) is 1.0/1.9/2.5 V max and Q10A must sink ~14 uA through the TPS3840's 100 kOhm internal MR pull-up at VGS ~= 2.0 V, Q10B runs at 0.990 x SW, and Q9B opens the low-battery LED at /D1A ~= 3.0 V. A worst-case part is at or below threshold in all three, so the brownout latch may never arm and the low-battery LED may never light -- invisibly, since the console works normally until the protection was meant to act. FDC6301N is 0.65/0.85/1.5 V max on the identical SUPERSOT-6 land with the same pin assignment, giving >=0.5 V of worst-case overdrive everywhere. Its asymmetric -0.5 V gate rating is covered by its own integrated gate-source Zener ('>6 kV HBM'), whose clamp current at Q10A's power-up excursion is set by R16 -- which ECO-8 had already raised from 10k to 100k, making it 25 uA. Headroom: 25 V / 0.22 A against 5.0 V and <=165 uA.

ECO-13. VOUT5 feedback top leg on U5. Left at 1% deliberately -- see ECO-13 section 13.7, which records the precision question as an OPEN follow-up rather than answering it blind: the argument that justified 0.1% on the LTC3527 was that converter's specified 50 nA feedback input current, and this fork has not read the equivalent number for the TPS63802.
ECO-13. Both TPS63802 feedback bottom legs. 1%, see R59.
ECO-13. VOUT3 feedback top leg on U13. 1%, see R59.
ECO-13. The /RESET RC with C30. Generic value, resolved from the AGBM-02 README.

ECO-13. TPS63802 feedforward caps. TDK CGA -- the automotive-qualified grade of the C-series, X7R 50 V, matching the family ECO-10 chose for the decoupling so the board stays on as few dielectric systems as possible.
ECO-13. Converter input bulk on VCC. Takes the same soft-termination 25 V part ECO-10 already chose for every other 10 uF placement.
ECO-13. Converter output bulk. Same soft-termination 25 V family as the rest of the 22 uF line.

ECO-13. A GAP IN MOUSEBITELABS' OWN BOM: C70 and C71 are fitted (not DNP) on both AGBM-01 and AGBM-02, and neither README lists them, so there is no upstream link to resolve. They are the 27 pF coupling caps on the hotkey touch-input nets -- Net-(C70-Pad1) is C70.1, R70.2, TP10.1, Z57.2 -- read off the netlist. C0G/NP0 is the right dielectric for a coupling cap whose value is the point. CHOSEN AGAINST THE FAMILIES THIS BOARD OTHERWISE USES, and here is why not: TDK's CGA3E2C0G1H270J080AA is the AEC-Q200 part that would match ECO-10's decoupling choice, but Mouser shows 8 in stock; Murata's GCM1885C1H270JA16D and GRM1885C1H270JA01D are both flagged Not Recommended for New Designs; TDK's C1608C0G1H270J080AA is Obsolete. The Samsung part is active with 174,716 at Mouser, $0.13 (Mouser figures, verified 2026-08-19 -- Digi-Key was rate-limiting during this lookup and reported nothing, which means UNKNOWN, not unavailable).
